stem: You are the transplant coordinator taking an after-hours call from a recipient. A 61-year-old liver transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. This is a routine long-term follow-up visit. The recipient is otherwise cooperative and wants guidance consistent with transplant references. Based on standard teaching about when to contact the transplant team, what is the MOST appropriate coordinator instruction?

Treat this as a non-urgent matter to discuss at the next medication refill request

Defer contact until temperature exceeds 40°C (104°F)

rationale_incorrect.C: Recipients should not independently stop immunosuppression; infection evaluation requires coordinated management.
rationale_incorrect.D: Urgent contact is indicated for infection symptoms without waiting for extreme fever thresholds.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator reviewing results in post-transplant clinic. A 52-year-old solid-organ transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. The patient is in the first post-transplant month. Nursing escalated the question before the attending signs orders. When teaching signs of post-transplant bacterial infection, which wound-related finding aligns with standard references?

options.text: Wound dehiscence
Wound dehiscence never indicates possible infection
Only fever above 104°F can accompany wound complications
Wound dehiscence is a normal expected finding that requires no evaluation

explanation.rationale_correct: Signs of bacterial infection include wound dehiscence along with wound erythema, purulent drainage, tenderness, and swelling.

rationale_incorrect.B: Wound dehiscence is listed among bacterial-infection signs requiring evaluation.
rationale_incorrect.C: Fever is usually ≥101°F (38.5°C), and wound dehiscence may occur with or without high fever.
rationale_incorrect.D: Wound dehiscence warrants clinical evaluation rather than being dismissed as always benign.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator rounding on the transplant unit. A 48-year-old solid-organ transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. The patient is in the first post-transplant month. Nursing escalated the question before the attending signs orders. When coordinating care for a transplant recipient with an infected surgical wound, which wound-management principle aligns with standard bacterial-infection references?

options.text: Wound treatment varies based on wound type, depth, drainage, progression of granulation tissue, and location
All wound infections are managed identically regardless of depth or drainage
Wound care never considers granulation tissue progression
Antibiotics alone replace all local wound management in every case

explanation.rationale_correct: Wound infection management includes appropriate antibiotics based on culture and sensitivities, with wound treatment varying by wound type, extent and depth, drainage, progression of granulation tissue, and location.

rationale_incorrect.B: Wound management is individualized rather than identical for all infections.
rationale_incorrect.C: Granulation tissue progression is among factors guiding wound treatment.
rationale_incorrect.D: Local wound care is individualized in addition to antibiotics rather than being replaced by antibiotics alone in every case.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator rounding on the transplant unit. A 48-year-old solid-organ transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. This is a routine long-term follow-up visit. The recipient is otherwise cooperative and wants guidance consistent with transplant references. When counseling a recently transplanted recipient about fungal infection risk, which timing pattern aligns with standard references?

options.text: Fungal infections usually occur in the early postoperative period
Fungal infections occur only after ten years post-transplant
Fungal infections are limited exclusively to the pretransplant period
Fungal infections never occur in the first year after transplant

explanation.rationale_correct: Fungal infections are less common than bacterial infections but usually occur in the early postoperative period, especially when risk factors such as surgical complications or indwelling catheters are present.

rationale_incorrect.B: Early postoperative timing is described rather than exclusive occurrence after a decade.
rationale_incorrect.C: Fungal infections are a post-transplant concern rather than being limited to pretransplant.
rationale_incorrect.D: Early postoperative occurrence is specifically noted rather than being absent in the first year.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator leading discharge planning for a recipient going home tomorrow. A 55-year-old solid-organ transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. This is a routine long-term follow-up visit. The recipient is otherwise cooperative and wants guidance consistent with transplant references. Which medication-safety step aligns with standard references?

options.text: Monitor tacrolimus levels carefully and adjust the dose as needed during fluconazole therapy
No tacrolimus level monitoring is needed because fluconazole does not affect calcineurin inhibitors
Stop tacrolimus permanently whenever any antifungal is prescribed
Double the tacrolimus dose automatically without laboratory monitoring

explanation.rationale_correct: Fluconazole increases tacrolimus levels, so tacrolimus levels must be monitored carefully and the dose adjusted as needed during fluconazole therapy.

rationale_incorrect.B: Fluconazole specifically increases tacrolimus levels rather than having no interaction.
rationale_incorrect.C: Tacrolimus continues with careful monitoring and dose adjustment rather than being stopped permanently.
rationale_incorrect.D: Dose changes require monitoring and individualized adjustment rather than automatic doubling without labs.

stem: You are the transplant coordinator taking an after-hours call from a recipient. A 61-year-old kidney transplant patient is the focus of today's interaction. No renal monitoring is needed because amphotericin never affects kidney function
Tacrolimus should be permanently discontinued before any antifungal therapy

rationale_incorrect.C: Tacrolimus continues with careful renal monitoring rather than being permanently stopped.

stem: You are teaching new staff about early post-kidney-transplant urinary complications. Attendees will apply the material when fielding recipient calls. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Genitourinary infection is the most common complication after kidney transplantation.
Surgical complications such as urine leaks and lymphoceles can predispose to bacterial superinfection.
Genitourinary infection is rare in the immediate post-transplant period.
Female sex is among patient factors that predispose to post-transplant UTI.

options.text: I and II only
I, II, and IV only
II and III only
I, II, III, and IV

explanation.rationale_correct: UTI is the most common kidney transplant complication, surgical issues such as leaks and lymphoceles predispose to superinfection, and female sex increases UTI risk. Statement III is false because early post-transplant UTI risk is substantial, not rare.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also true—female sex is listed among predisposing factors.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement III is false; early UTI risk is significant.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false; not all four statements are correct.

stem: You are updating long-term malignancy-prevention teaching. Statements will be checked against textbook and policy anchors. Evaluate the following statements:

stem: An adult kidney transplant recipient has delayed graft function attributed to acute tubular necrosis (ATN) without rejection or obstruction. Statements will be checked against textbook and policy anchors. Evaluate the following clinical statements:

elements.text: Increased blood urea nitrogen and creatinine may be present.
Anuria or oliguria may occur.
Pulmonary edema is a characteristic isolated sign that always distinguishes ATN from other causes.
Elevated potassium and magnesium levels may occur.

options.text: I and II only
I, II, and IV only
III and IV only
I, II, III, and IV

explanation.rationale_correct: ATN presents as renal failure in the absence of rejection or obstruction with increased BUN/creatinine, anuria or oliguria, and elevated potassium and magnesium. Pulmonary edema is not listed among the characteristic ATN signs in the source question set.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement IV is also correct—elevated potassium and magnesium are listed ATN signs.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statements I and II are also true; statement III overstates pulmonary edema as a distinguishing isolated ATN sign.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement III is false as stated—pulmonary edema is not among the listed characteristic ATN signs.

stem: You are reviewing deceased-donor infection-prevention protocols with the procurement team. Statements will be checked against textbook and policy anchors. Evaluate the following statements about donor-transmitted infections:

elements.text: Donor-transmitted infection can cause significant recipient morbidity and mortality.
Unexpected donor-to-recipient infection transmission never occurs after transplantation.
Donor chart review is part of donor risk assessment.
Donor physical examination may reveal track marks suggesting recent drug use.

options.text: I and II only
I, III, and IV only
II, III, and IV only
I, II, III, and IV

explanation.rationale_correct: Donor-transmitted infections may cause significant morbidity and mortality; donor chart review and physical examination including track marks are standard risk-assessment steps. Unexpected transmission can still occur, so statement II is false.

rationale_incorrect.A: Statement II is false; statements III and IV are also correct.
rationale_incorrect.C: Statement I is also true; statement II is false.
rationale_incorrect.D: Statement II is false—unexpected donor-to-recipient infection transmission remains an infrequent but recognized complication.

stem: You are updating visitor infection-prevention teaching on the transplant unit. Attendees will apply the material when fielding recipient calls. Evaluate the following statements:

elements.text: Family members and visitors should wash their hands well before and after contact with the patient.
Visitors should cover their mouth and nose when coughing and sneezing.
Visitors with illness should have unrestricted close contact without any precautions.
Sanitizing hand gel may be used when soap and water are not immediately available.
